added.name: Dualizer
added.long_description:
Dualizer builds AI-powered, physics-based process simulation and digital twins to design and scale chemical processes and optimize existing plants. We help engineering teams identify bottlenecks, increase yield and throughput, and reduce energy and production costs—improving plant efficiency and profitability.

The platform combines AI reasoning, our proprietary deterministic simulation and optimization engine, and physics-informed machine learning. Engineers can build, calibrate, and refine models through conversation, starting from a diagram, available data, or an engineering objective. Calculations account for thermodynamics, material and energy balances, equipment behavior, and operating constraints, enabling teams to optimize interconnected equipment and operating conditions across a plant.

Equipment sizing and costing, 3D layout planning, and techno-economic analysis connect process improvements to plant-level decisions. Teams can accelerate new process scale-up, debottleneck operating plants, and continually refine operating strategies as production targets and plant conditions change. Dualizer makes rigorous simulation and optimization an ongoing capability for improving industrial productivity and profitability throughout a plant’s life.
added.one_liner: AI-powered physical simulation to design/optimize chemical processes

long_description.before:
At Latent, we're building medical language models to tackle the trillions of operational overhead weighing down healthcare. Our flagship product streamlines authorizations for life-saving drugs by analyzing EHR records and surfacing the most relevant data.

We've built our product and signed enterprise contracts with some of the largest health systems in the US.
long_description.after:
In the U.S., the path between experiencing a health problem and completing treatment is much more complicated than it should be.

Many people have conditions no one catches, or qualify for a therapy no one offers them. Others wait weeks for insurance approval, or start treatment and drop off. As complex new therapies reach the market faster, the problem will get worse.

Latent builds AI for health system pharmacy teams, the people responsible for getting patients on treatment and helping them complete it. Today, pharmacy teams spend hours every week digging through charts, insurance portals, and payer rules, and going back and forth with insurers. They’re already stretched thin, and health systems can’t hire their way out.

Our clinical AI reads the patient chart, the insurance requirements, and the drug label, then does the work pharmacy teams don’t have time for. It flags patients whose charts point to an untreated condition, gets their therapy approved, and helps each person follow through with their care.

More than 70 U.S. health systems use Latent across more than 5 million patient medication journeys a year. We believe intelligent systems can help every breakthrough medicine reach every patient it is made for. If you want to build AI that changes lives, talk to us.

one_liner.before: Medical language models to automate healthcare operations
one_liner.after: Clinical AI that gets life-changing medicine to the people who need it

long_description.before:
Elip is an AI agent for careers and for hiring.

Candidates send their resume once and say what they want next, and what they'd never take. Each morning Elip reads every new role and sends a few that fit, each with the reason it fits and what's missing. The rest is set aside. When a role is right, Elip tailors the resume for it and the candidate approves every change. Elip is free for candidates, and they can hide their profile from any employer they choose.

Companies book a call and tell Elip the role. Within minutes of the call they get a shortlist of people who fit, each with the reason. They pay 10% of first-year base salary, only when they hire, with a full refund if the hire resigns or is let go for performance or conduct within three months. No fee for someone they were already talking to.

Elip is based in San Francisco.

Where Elip is going: soon your agent will look for your next job, and a company's agent will look for its next hire. Elip is where the agents meet.
long_description.after:
Elip sends you the jobs a friend would send you, and gives a company the shortlist a friend would write.

For people: add your resume and say what you want and what you'd never take. Each morning Elip reads millions of jobs from across the internet with that in mind. It sets aside what you said no to and sends the few that fit, each with why and what's missing. Some mornings, none. When one is right, Elip rewrites your resume for that role and you approve every change. Free.

For companies: tell Elip the role. Within minutes you get a short list of people who fit, each with the reason. You meet once they say yes, and pay 10% of first-year base salary only when you hire. Nobody can pay to appear on a shortlist.

Where Elip is going: a world where nobody has to start from zero with a stranger.

Elip is based in San Francisco.

one_liner.before: AI agent for careers and hiring: the few that fit, with the reason.
one_liner.after: Jobs a friend would send you, and a shortlist a friend would write.

long_description.before: RunAnywhere runs open-weight models at full speed wherever a company needs them. Wally is our inference stack for open models: serverless inference, BYOC, or on-prem, so code and data never leave their network. One command puts a Wally-served model inside Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, etc. When a model fits on the device, the same tooling runs it locally through our open-source SDKs for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux, and web, built on kernels written by our agentic harness for Apple and Qualcomm silicon (10K+ GitHub stars).
long_description.after:
Inference research at the frontier. Our agents build the kernels for each chip, and Wally ships the tokens.

We're RunAnywhere (YC W26), a research-led inference company, and you can use frontier open models like GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and MiniMax M3 on Wally today. Wally has an OpenAI-compatible API and the wally CLI, with zero data retention by default, and it works with OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and Cline. Tell your agent: set up https://runanywhere.ai/SKILL.md

For AWS Trainium, trnRT is our open-source (Apache-2.0) LLM inference engine. Aman Swar and Sanchit Monga's post covers serving GLM-5.3-Flash on one Trainium2 box: https://runanywhere.ai/blog/glm-5-3-flash-trainium2-nki-megakernels

For on-device AI, the open-source RunAnywhere SDKs share a C++ core across Swift, Kotlin, React Native, Flutter, TypeScript and C++.

We publish how we measured each result, so you can judge whether it applies to your workload. Happy to help any YC founder running coding agents, long-context workloads or on-device models.

one_liner.before: Fastest inference anywhere: open models on-prem, hosted or on-device
one_liner.after: Inference research at the frontier. Frontier open models on Wally.

long_description.after:
Current is an opinionated way to work with your coding agents. It lets you run hundreds of agents while staying in control.

The problem with running agents in parallel isn't their intelligence. It's your attention. You end up scrolling walls of text and tool calls, looking for answers you'd already been given.

So Current drops the chat entirely and focuses on your agents' outputs, not their inputs. Everything is an issue, from a quick fix to a big project with sub-issues. You write it, and your agents pick it up and deliver.

When they're done, they notify you and show you what they made: a report, a chart, a before and after video, or an interactive app that shows their work. You review the work, not how they got there. Comment and the agent goes back to work. Approve and it merges.

Current is built with Current. It's free on Mac, Windows, Linux and iPhone, and works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and many more agents.

one_liner.before: Create & play AI games with friends
one_liner.after: Run hundreds of coding agents and stay in control

OpenCrawl is an open-source platform that lets AI coding agents work as a team.

Engineering teams now run many agents at once, across Claude Code, Codex, laptops, and cloud environments. Each one works alone, so engineers spend their time moving context between agents and cleaning up duplicated work and conflicting changes.

Ordo Labs is bringing AI into regulated labs. In paid pilots with labs in the US and Europe, Ordo cut post-analysis work by 90%+.

CROs and CDMOs are a $314.8B industry, but they can't rely on generic AI tools, because every result must be traceable, every system validated, and every change QA-approved. Ordo is the AI-native OS for regulated labs: each lab gets its own deployment built to be validated, every output links back to its source data, and scientists and QA sign off on every result. Every workflow on Ordo inherits these controls.

Live today: data analysis, quality review and reporting. We're advised by laboratory executives and have interviewed 100+ scientists. Our goal is to make regulated labs AI-native, so science can move at the speed of AI.

Run a CRO or CDMO? Email us at founders@ordolabs.ai.
long_description.after:
Ordo lets regulated labs delegate analysis, quality checks and report drafting to AI agents. We turn each lab’s checking rules into workflows, with source-linked results for scientists to review and approve.

We have two paid pilots with labs in the US and Europe. Pilot results show 90%+ less time spent on post-analysis work.

Our ambition is to make lab software perform more of the work scientists currently do manually, expanding across analytical methods, report types and sites.

Agents do the work, scientists sign.

ORO AI is an applied AI research lab. We build high-fidelity simulation environments grounded in real data to teach AI the tacit knowledge required to run safe and profitable autonomous businesses.

Our first public benchmark, SMB Bench, puts a frontier model in charge of a produce wholesaler's buying desk for a simulated 90-day quarter, where shortages and supplier failures have delayed effects. The report, leaderboard and every run are available: https://oroagents.com/benchmarks/smb-bench

SMB Bench is a step toward our longer-term goal of having AI as an independent economic actor that can safely run profitable businesses.

Physical validation is the main bottleneck of scientific research agents. Existing labs already have capacity, yet experiments remain difficult to access and coordinate. Halmos Labs plans experiments, and enables access to physical validation. Connecting to Halmos, every agent can close the loop on R&D without leaving the terminal.
long_description.after:
The drug development pipeline is built around humans. Other AI biotech companies build automation around the established infrastructure. Halmos Labs rebuilds the infrastructure around automation. The central bottleneck is access to experiments. Halmos Labs platform physicalvalidation.com connects agents to biolabs across the globe in days rather than weeks. 

Using physicalvalidation.com, Halmos research agent is continuously designing drugs and has so far designed and tested a new mRNA cancer vaccine and a new antibiotic with results December 10th.

one_liner.after: Rebuilding drug development for automation

long_description.before:
Graphide CI runs your CI 10-20× faster than GitHub runners, and our 24/7 agents optimize the CI itself, not just the machines. For teams with big CI bills that haven't been optimized, we cut costs 70%+ and take over the ongoing work of optimizing CI, so you can focus on your product.

We're faster and cheaper because we own both the hardware and the optimizations and configs that run on it, which lets us do what owning only one could not. A graph of the codebase runs only the tests each change can reach, and we run your tests in parallel, so your CI is limited only by the length of your longest test. Our agents then tune machines, caches and test splits as you add more tests and code over time. We also patch the tests themselves, fixing flakes and adding our own libraries so they run faster and more reliably.

Coding agents now write more code than teams can check, making verification the new bottleneck. CI is where we start, but we also cover the rest of the verification stack. Our PR review agent runs the old and new code in live environments, finding bugs and proving them by writing tests (50% more bugs found than Greptile on our benchmarks, with 35% fewer false positives). Our visualizer shows data flows and graph-based diffs so you can understand a PR in seconds.
